[TASK: 2560x1440 2K QHD 16:9 ARCHITECTURAL RELIGHTING & STATIC RECONSTRUCTION]
Transform the reference photogrammetry plate into a razor-sharp, photorealistic 6x7 medium-format architectural survey photograph.

MANDATORY TRANSFORMATION RULES:
1. PLANAR RECTIFICATION & GEOMETRY LOCK: Treat the reference image as an immutable spatial coordinate frame. Eliminate all 3D mesh polygon wobble, melted facades, and distorted rooflines. Plumb all vertical walls to true gravity vertical. Render razor-sharp ashlar courses, straight timber sash mullions, and crisp slate roofs.
2. STATIC DECLUTTERING (MANDATORY): COMPLETELY ERASE all transient vehicles, parked cars, delivery vans, pedestrians, and temporary street clutter from the seed image. Repaint the carriageway with authentic road surfacing, stone setts, whinstone kerbs, and clean flagstone pavements.
3. BOTANICAL PHENOLOGY & CANOPY INTEGRITY: Overwrite all raw 3D mesh blob foliage with authentic seasonal canopy structures matching the target date. Zero green summer foliage during dormant/autumn/winter periods:
   - Botanical Composition: Urban canopy of mature broadleaf specimens within the central private pleasure garden (Moray Place Gardens), including *Acer pseudoplatanus* (Sycamore), *Ulmus glabra* (Wych Elm), *Tilia × europaea* (Common Lime), and *Fraxinus excelsior* (European Ash), bordered by *Ilex aquifolium* (Holly) perimeter hedgerows.
- Seasonal Phenology (November): Late-autumn dormancy; broadleaf canopies mostly defoliated revealing intricate, bare dark-timber branch architectures, with sparse clusters of desiccated yellow-brown and bronze senescent foliage remaining on sheltered inner limbs and a blanket of fallen leaf litter over maintained turf.
4. OPTICAL DEPTH: Pin-sharp infinite depth of field (f/11). Zero lens blur, tilt-shift, or depth-of-field falloff across foreground and background.

[SOLAR & ATMOSPHERIC LIGHTING OVERRIDE]
SOLAR LIGHT VECTOR (4500K Late afternoon raking sunlight with warm golden highlights): Sun at camera-left (Azimuth 202.9°, Elevation 14.2°). left walls in direct sun, right walls in deep shadow. long lateral shadows project across ground to RIGHT.

[SCENE GEOMETRY & AUTHENTIC LITHICS]
Medium format architectural documentary photograph of Moray Place, Edinburgh. Elevated perspective capturing the monumental 1822 Georgian duodecagonal circus by James Gillespie Graham. Symmetrical palace-fronted terraces built of cream-buff Craigleith sandstone with polished ashlar finish and channelled V-joint rustication on ground floors. Structural vertical lines plumbed true. Fenestration ordered in rigorous grids of 6-over-6 and 8-over-8 timber sash-and-case windows set in precise reveals, with cast-iron anthemion-and-palmette balconettes and perimeter spearhead railings fronting sunken stone basements. Steep Scottish slate hipped roofs with lead hips, moulded cornices, and heavy ashlar chimney stacks. Central communal parkland enclosed by cast-iron railings, populated by mature Acer pseudoplatanus, Ulmus glabra, and Tilia × europaea in mid-November phenology: bare, defoliated branch silhouettes, trace russet and amber foliage remnants, and leaf-strewn green lawn. Roadway of smooth dark macadam bounded by historic whinstone kerbstones and flagstone pavements. Authentic historic masonry patina with localized soot accumulations in cornices, ferrous stone veining, and micro-greening at plinth bases. Pure architectural stillness, completely devoid of vehicles, pedestrians, and street clutter.
